You can actually see the speed of sound as Queen fans move when they hear the music beat
It is basically a faint shimmer you see move quickly through the crowd.
Through the crowd, away from the stage/speakers if you're still having trouble. It actually happens several times.

Watch the crowd's hands. It's a wave from front to back.

I'm guessing this is mostly due to them probably having speakers set up both at the front and somewhere towards the back of the venue that are slightly out of sync.

In this picture I'm not seeing any delay speakers set up. So all of the sound is likely coming out of the normal PA by the stage, hence you can see the effect in this gif.

Most concerts these days that have a "deep" crowd like this will have speakers somewhere around the halfway point (or even more sets throughout) that are on just enough of a time-delay that the sound coming out of them reaches the ears of the audience at the same time that the original sound from the PA is hitting them.

Since the speed of sound is ~1125 feet per second, you can figure out exactly how much delay you need.

Actually, having the delay wouldn't change this "wave" effect that we're getting in this picture, since it's still taking time to reach all the way to the back.

Have you ever taken a break from all internet/social media? How did it go?

My phone died once when I was away from home, if that counts.

It was terrible.
It was called the 90's and it sucked balls

Every year for the last 6 years I spend a week disconnected - zero phone, internet, TV, electronics of any type. The only thing I don't give up is music. It's freaking awesome. You actually have to find something to do or talk to people face to face. i also drink a lot of wine during that week.

I had to sorta quit Tumblr; was following a lot of levelheaded smart people (some of them awesome artists), but got addicted to scrolling.

I miss my friends and the other interesting people; but the way the site works was harmful to my sanity and free time.

Took a month off to drive around the states and go camping.

It was no big deal at all. I didn't feel suddenly unburdened or lonely or free or whatever. It was very uneventful. When I decided to boot social media back up a few people said welcome back but mostly it was just back to normal.

And the Internet just had some new memes but was almost exactly the same as a month ago.
William Gibson calls the practice a "media fast". It's a good thing.

I did it a few years ago for 2 months. It was pretty awesome. I was stress free, relaxed, and not even a bit depressed. Even stopped drinking completely because I just didn't feel like it. Got laid a lot more and spent a lot more time with people, made a lot of friends, etc. I also re-sparked my interest in books, reading, and music. Ended up reading a few books and listening to the BBC version of the foundation series which I always put off since I assumed it was meh and outdated. I loved it.

I think the biggest change was that I was no longer afraid of taking that first step when it came to doing new things. I was always scared before, or felt ashamed in some way. Without the internet, and running out of shit to do, I started giving less of a fuck. I started doing things I never imagined myself doing, and was less afraid of trying new things.

So I guess it went pretty well.
